description: Curated SecHub Resources SC4S pack for common Linux /var/log and syslog relay records, with fixture-backed routing for sshd authentication failure/success, sudo command execution, su/PAM session and authentication failure, cron execution, kernel messages, systemd service state, syslog-wrapped package-manager changes, and shadow-utils account/group lifecycle rows.

event_families.label: Linux syslog-wrapped package manager change messages

timestamp_policy.notes: Fixtures use RFC3164-style month/day/time payload timestamps with no timezone/year. The send helper wraps fixtures with timezone-qualified RFC5424 timestamps for replay.

field_delimiting.quote_character: double quote around synthetic marker; sudo uses semicolon-separated key/value segments
field_delimiting.escape_policy: Synthetic values avoid secrets and use RFC5737 documentation addresses
field_delimiting.notes: Each line is one OS syslog message. Multiline application logs are outside this initial pack.

source.reference: Public Linux/OpenSSH/sudo/cron/systemd/kernel syslog conventions, Linux-PAM templates, Debian/Red Hat package log docs, and shadow-utils account/group lifecycle syslog templates.
source.notes: Fixtures use generic hostnames/users/groups and RFC5737 documentation IP addresses; no customer Linux syslog records or proprietary TA content are included.

curation.notes: Selected from Milestone 8 P0 operating-system telemetry backlog after Windows Event Log and Linux auditd. Initial scope is conservative common syslog relay coverage, not full Linux TA compatibility or field validation.

pack_variants.label: RFC3164-style Linux program syslog relay
pack_variants.description: Default initial variant for one common Linux OS syslog message per line, optionally syslog-wrapped by a collector relay.
known_limitations: Synthetic-equivalent fixtures only; no live Linux syslog relay capture or Splunk read-back.

Distro/collector variants, PAM modules beyond documented `su` session/auth-failure examples, broader shadow-utils variants beyond the fixture-backed create/delete/shell-change rows, native non-syslog package log files, journald JSON, and multiline application logs are not covered in this pack.

cribl.notes: Use only after sampling the actual Linux syslog relay schema. Do not drop command, user, host, source, service, or marker context by default.

vector.notes: Vector support is recorded as a conservative sources/transforms/sinks mapping only: native syslog listener or relay-to-syslog path; preserve the pack sourcetype/source routing and validate listener framing locally. No Vector config artifact is generated by this pack yet.

fluent_bit.notes: Fluent Bit support is recorded as a conservative collector/pipeline mapping only: native syslog listener or relay-to-syslog path; preserve the pack sourcetype/source routing and validate listener framing locally. No Fluent Bit config artifact is generated by this pack yet.

validation_commands: Import exported NDJSON into a disposable OpenSearch Dashboards space and confirm data view/index-pattern resolution.
opensearch_dashboards.notes: OpenSearch Dashboards support is recorded as visualization-target metadata only. Splunk dashboards, where present, have not been automatically translated to OpenSearch saved objects or live-tested.

known_limitations: No live Linux syslog relay, SC4S runtime replay, HEC delivery, Splunk read-back, Manager apply, or production evidence captured.
Synthetic-equivalent fixtures are documentation-shaped and do not prove source validation.

Parser routes selected common OS families only; PAM modules beyond the documented `su` session/auth-failure examples, broader shadow-utils variants beyond the fixture-backed create/delete/shell-change rows, native non-syslog package log files, journald JSON, distro-specific wrappers, and multiline application logs remain future work.
RFC3164-style payload timestamps lack timezone/year unless wrapped by a timezone-qualified relay envelope.
